subject: FintechCo / Redwood - API auth & key management follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: FintechCo / Redwood - API auth & key management follow-up

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo and the time today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope the technical deep-dive with our SEs:

Recap (what we heard)
- You want to embed Redwood into two flows: (1) backend ingestion + embedding generation for search/rerank, (2) user-facing generation + tool-calling.
- Primary concerns: authentication model, key rotation, and how service accounts vs user-scoped tokens should be handled.
- Compliance: Samira's security team will want details on key storage, rotation, and audit logs.

Questions / asks for the deep-dive
1) What auth method do you prefer for server-to-server calls (API keys vs OAuth2 client credentials / signed JWTs)?
2) Do you need tokens scoped per-product (separate keys for embeddings vs generation)?
3) Rotation policy: what cadence (30/90/180 days) and who manages rotation (FintechCo KMS or Redwood-managed keys)?
4) Routing/region requirements: any strict data residency or routing per-region headers we should honor?
5) Tool-calling & structured output: will you require function-calling with restricted scopes or separate service accounts per integration?

Attached: redwood-sdk-auth-flow.png (high-level flow), fintechco-sso-reqs.pdf (from today), and a draft rotation spreadsheet we maintain.

Next steps
- Rishi (SE) to run a technical deep-dive (30-45m) to propose concrete auth flows + SDK examples.
- Samira to share any security questionnaire items that must be answered before POC.
- We'll share a short proposal with recommended rotation cadence and an implementation checklist after the call.

Proposed times for SE deep-dive: Tue 2028-07-25 11:00-11:45 PT or Wed 2028-07-26 09:00-09:45 PT. Which works for you + Samira?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is great, appreciate the clear recap. A few answers from our side to help Rishi prepare:

High level preferences
- For server-to-server (ingestion + backend calls) we prefer API keys tied to service accounts. Our infra team currently rotates symmetric API keys via our KMS and publishes public key material for verification.
- For user-scoped access (when we act on behalf of a logged-in user) security prefers OAuth2 / signed JWTs (we can mint via our IdP).
- We do use separate projects for embeddings vs generation in order to isolate costs, so scoped keys per-product would be ideal.

Rotation & KMS
- Our standard rotation cadence is 90 days for symmetric keys, but for high-sensitivity flows we sometimes do 30 days.
- We can integrate with Redwood-managed rotation if you support bringing-your-own-KMS (BYOK). If not, we will push rotated keys from our KMS via API.

Other constraints
- Regional routing: US-only for PG data; EU for EU customers. We'd like a header-based routing option (e.g., x-redwood-region: eu/us) to hit regional endpoints.
- For function-calling we need scoped tokens that limit which external tools can be invoked (security wants least-privilege).

Samira will send over our security questionnaire + SOC evidence next (cc'd). We'll take the Tue/Wed times and I'll confirm once I sync Samira's calendar.

Alex

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-23T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo / Redwood - API auth & key management follow-up

Thanks Alex — great context. I pulled together a recommended approach and a few options so we can make the deep-dive efficient. TL;DR: support both models, but we recommend short-lived JWTs for user-scoped flows and project-bound API keys + BYOK for server-to-server. Details below.

Options (summary)
1) API keys (server-to-server) — simplest to integrate
   - Scoped to a Redwood project and optionally to an API surface (embeddings vs generation).
   - Rotation: supported via our Keys API; we can accept rotated key material pushed from your KMS or manage rotation ourselves if you enable BYOK integration.
   - Revocation: immediate via Key ID; audit logs are stored for 365 days by default (SLA add-on available).

2) OAuth2 / signed JWTs (user-scoped) — recommended for end-user actions
   - Your IdP mints short-lived JWTs (exp 5-15m); Redwood validates signature (we support RS256/ES256).
   - Optionally bind tokens to a service account to allow delegation without exchanging long-lived keys.

3) Service accounts + asymmetric keys
   - Support for asymmetric (public key) verification if you prefer not to transmit symmetric material. Redwood accepts public keys and stores key metadata; rotation handled via key versioning.

Key rotation plan (suggested)
- Symmetric API keys: 90-day rotation default. We recommend staged rollover: create new key, switch ingestion jobs to new key during maintenance window, revoke old key after 24-48h.
- For high-sensitivity endpoints (tool-calling, payments-related prompts) use 30-day rotation and enforce shorter TTLs on tokens.
- We'll provide a sample rotation playbook (attached) and a webhook-based health check to verify key deployment.

Routing & regional controls
- Header-based routing supported: use x-redwood-region: eu/us and we will route to regional clusters. We also support explicit region in the SDK config.

Embeddings / reranker considerations
- Recommend separate service accounts / keys for ingestion (embedding creation) vs query-time reranking to isolate costs and revoke access granularly.
- We can also provide scoped API keys that only allow /embeddings endpoints.

Tool-calling & structured output
- Function-calling requires the calling token to have the function-call scope. We can issue scoped tokens per service account to limit capabilities.

Attachments included: redwood-sdk-auth-flow.png (flow diagram) and redwood-rotation-plan.xlsx (sample schedule + rollforward steps). Also linking our docs for reference: https://redwood.app/docs/authentication

If this looks good, I propose we run the SE deep-dive on Tue 2028-07-25 11:00 PT (30-45m). Agenda:
- 10m: Review FintechCo constraints (Samira)
- 20m: Walk through proposed auth flows + rotation playbook (me)
- 10-15m: Q&A + next steps (Marissa + Vivek)

Thanks — Rishi
